title: Problem Definition and Requirements
definition: Problem definition establishes the required outcome, stakeholders, inputs, outputs, constraints, and acceptance boundaries before a solution is designed.
purpose: Prevent solution-first implementation by making the problem and success boundary inspectable.
history: Requirements and systems engineering formalized stakeholder needs, requirements, acceptance, and traceability; this record provides the beginner-facing boundary.
mental_model: A problem contract is the shared boundary between an observed need and later solution design.
analogy: A destination and travel constraints must be known before selecting a route; the analogy stops because software stakeholders and requirements can conflict and change.
common_mistakes: Writing a technology choice as the problem
industry_notes: Teams use bounded requirements and acceptance evidence to align product, engineering, test, security, and operations.
ai_notes: AI may clarify wording but cannot invent authoritative requirements; every added requirement needs source and review.
interview_notes: Ask how the candidate would clarify an ambiguous ticket before coding.
exercise_candidates: Turn a solution-first request into a problem contract
lab_candidates: Decompose a ticket-pricing request into contract fields
project_candidates: Create the problem contract for the first project increment
